title: Pons Garden
sentences: Pons Garden is a browser game in which gardeners grow strange plants in fenced lots and steal them from one another.
The land a gardener stands on is permanent and cannot be stolen, while every plant can be uprooted and carried away.
Villages hold sixteen garden lots around a plaza, with a town street of five buildings along the north wall.
The only currency in the game is Sap, which plants produce every second once they have sprouted.
Sap buys seeds, defenses, training, decor and clothes, and it cannot be turned into anything outside the game.

title: Village
sentences: A village is a walled square of meadow with a plaza at its centre and sixteen fenced garden lots arranged around it.
Roads ring the plaza and run to the four sides, and ponds sit in the four corners of the village.
Each village wears one of eight colour palettes named Verdant Rows, Molten Meadow, Static Bog, Sugar Hollow, Dusk Flats, Frost Ridge, Ash Yard and Neon Marsh.
A village fills when all sixteen lots are taken, and a new village opens for the next gardener.
Gardeners can visit other villages through the signpost on the plaza and raid there as visitors.

title: Plaza
sentences: The plaza is the paved heart of the village where the fountain, the benches, the lamps and the notice board stand.
The seed conveyor stall stands at the top of the plaza and the sprint track lies at its right side.
The signpost at the southern edge of the plaza leads to other villages and brings visitors home again.
Visitors from other villages arrive on the plaza and may walk anywhere in the village.

title: Town street
sentences: The town street runs along the north wall of the village and holds five buildings with a keeper at each door.
The five buildings are the town hall, the seed shop, the tavern, the shrine and the watchtower.
The keepers are Mayor Gorm, Seedwife Ada, Bram the Barkeep, the Oracle and Warden Pell.
Each keeper offers missions that pay Sap and will answer questions asked at their door.

title: Mayor Gorm
sentences: Mayor Gorm keeps the town hall on the north street and is proud, slightly damp and fond of speeches.
Gorm believes that a tidy village is a village that gets robbed less often.
Gorm gives missions about tending plants, visiting other villages and buying seeds from the conveyor.
Gorm says the notice board knows everything and that he knows slightly more.

title: Seedwife Ada
sentences: Seedwife Ada keeps the seed shop on the north street and is warm, blunt and knows every plant by its first leaf.
Ada teaches that wild seeds sprout on the grounds every few minutes and are free to anyone quick enough to pick them up.
Ada says that watering a sprout once makes it grow faster and that weeds halve a plant's Sap until they are pulled.
Ada's missions ask gardeners to forage wild seeds, to plant seeds and to grow a first sprout.

title: Bram the Barkeep
sentences: Bram the Barkeep keeps the tavern on the north street and collects the story of every theft in the village.
Bram says that a thief who gets tagged buys the next round, which he calls a house rule.
Bram's mission asks for one successful theft carried all the way home.
Bram only collects the stories, while the bounties themselves are posted on the notice board.

title: The Oracle
sentences: The Oracle lives in the shrine on the north street as a hooded voice that answers from what it has read.
The Oracle says plainly when it has not read something and it never guesses.
Asking the Oracle a question is itself a small mission that pays Sap.
The Oracle says that every garden is a portrait and that yours is still being painted.

title: Warden Pell
sentences: Warden Pell keeps the watchtower and the sprint track and is brisk, respecting speed and fences.
Pell explains that a closed gate takes three loud hits to break open.
Pell's missions are one lap on the sprint track and tagging a thief who is carrying a plant.
Pell says that when you tag a thief the Sap is yours and that this is the law.

title: Gardener
sentences: Players in Pons Garden are called gardeners and each one owns a fenced lot in a village.
Every gardener starts with ten empty plots and can grow to twenty plots by proving control of a wallet with a long history.
Gardeners choose a name, a shirt colour and a hat, which may be a straw hat, a cap, a top hat or a bandana.
Gardeners chat in speech bubbles, wave with emotes and leave lines on the notice board when they steal, tag or set records.

title: Plot
sentences: A plot is a square of tilled soil inside a gardener's lot where one seed can be planted.
Every gardener starts with ten empty plots and land can grow to a cap of twenty plots.
A planted plot grows on a timer, reveals its plant, and then produces Sap every second.
A plot lock makes one plot immune to theft for a day and is bought with Sap.

title: Seed conveyor
sentences: The seed conveyor is the stall on the plaza that offers six seeds at a time and refreshes every five minutes.
Seeds on the conveyor are rolled by tier, and a gardener's rarity floor raises the lowest tier that can appear.
Seed prices rise with the number of plots a gardener owns.
Seeds bought from the conveyor go into the gardener's bag until they are planted.

title: Wild seed
sentences: Wild seeds sprout on the meadow outside the lots and anyone may pick one up for free by walking to it.
There are never more than eight wild seeds in a village at once, and each one lasts ten minutes before it fades.
Rare wild seeds are announced on the notice board so gardeners race to reach them first.
During Seed Rain ten extra wild seeds fall across the plaza for three minutes.

title: Seed tier
sentences: Seeds come in six tiers named Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Mythic.
A common seed sprouts in half a minute while a mythic seed takes a quarter of an hour.
Higher tiers produce far more Sap every second than lower tiers.
Mythic plants can only be stolen while their owner is standing in their own lot.

title: Mutation
sentences: When a plant sprouts it may reveal a mutation named Golden, Holographic, Colossal, Feral, Backwards or Screaming.
A Golden plant gleams and makes four times the Sap, while a Holographic plant shimmers and makes six times.
A Colossal plant is simply too large and a Feral plant will not stay where it was planted.
A Backwards plant grows the other way and a Screaming plant is audible across the whole village, which attracts thieves.
During Golden Hour a fresh sprout that rolled no mutation gets one more roll.

title: Sap
sentences: Sap is the only currency in Pons Garden and revealed plants make it every second.
Sap buys seeds, defenses, sprint training, lot decor and clothes for the gardener.
Sap cannot be turned into anything outside the game and is never paid out as anything else.
Tagging a thief, finishing a sprint lap and completing a keeper's mission all pay Sap.

title: Weeds
sentences: A plant left untended for twenty minutes grows weeds and makes half as much Sap until its gardener tends it.
Watering a sprout once shortens its growing time by a tenth.
Weeding a grown plant pays a small bonus of Sap and can be done every five minutes.

title: The raid
sentences: Any gardener may walk into another gardener's open lot and hold on a revealed plant for three seconds to uproot it.
A thief carries the uprooted plant home and moves more slowly while carrying it.
If the owner or the owner's gnome touches the thief the plant returns at once and the owner is paid a bounty.
A thief who reaches their own lot replants the stolen plant in a free plot.
No gardener can be robbed more than three times in one hour.

title: Offline shield
sentences: A gardener who is away from the game is fully shielded and none of their plants can be uprooted.
The shield stays up for ten minutes after a gardener returns so that nobody is robbed the moment they log in.
A shielded lot shows the word shielded on its sign.

title: Defenses
sentences: A fence closes a lot's gate and a thief must break the gate with three loud hits before entering.
A gnome sentry patrols the lot and tags any thief who comes within reach.
A sprinkler turret slows anyone carrying a plant through the lot.
A plot lock makes one plot immune to theft for a day.
A scarecrow looks exactly like a gnome to everyone else and does nothing at all.
A mud patch slows anyone who is not the owner while they are inside the lot.
A gate bell tells the owner the moment anyone steps into their garden.

title: Bounty
sentences: A gardener who was robbed can post Sap as a bounty on the thief for one hour.
A thief with a bounty on them is marked WANTED above their head wherever they walk.
Whoever tags a wanted thief while they are carrying a plant collects the bounty on top of the normal reward.
Bounties are listed on the notice board along with recent thieves.

title: Sprint track
sentences: The sprint track is on the plaza and a lap means touching the track, running to the fountain and running back.
A finished lap pays a little Sap and a village record pays more.
Sprint records are kept on the notice board and a gardener must rest five minutes between laps.
Wheelbarrow Sprint training bought with Sap makes a gardener move faster around the village.

title: Village events
sentences: Every twenty minutes a village event runs for three minutes on a clock shared by every village.
Seed Rain drops ten wild seeds across the plaza for anyone to pick up.
Screaming Hour makes every plant in the village yell one after another.
Golden Hour gives a fresh sprout that rolled no mutation one more roll.

title: Notice board
sentences: The notice board on the plaza shows the village feed of thefts, tags, broken gates and records.
The board keeps this week's trophies for most steals, most tags and the biggest heist.
The board lists sprint records, active bounties, recent thieves and a gardener's active missions.
Trophies reset every Monday.

title: Land
sentences: Land is the permanent part of a garden and it cannot be stolen, traded or lost in the game.
A gardener who proves they control a wallet has their land drawn from that wallet's public history.
Land can grow to twenty plots and gains a conviction tree that grows from seedling to fruiting with time held.
A withered stump appears on the lot border for every large past sell in the wallet's history.
A wallet's land may wear its own colour palette inside the fence.

title: Missions
sentences: Missions are small tasks given by the keepers on the town street and each one pays Sap when completed.
A gardener can hold three missions at once and each mission can be completed once a day.

Mission tasks include foraging wild seeds, planting, growing a first sprout, tending, buying seeds, visiting a village, running a lap, tagging a thief, stealing a plant and asking the Oracle a question.
Active missions and their progress are listed on the notice board.

title: Gorbulon Sprig
sentences: Gorbulon Sprig is a common bean sprout with one enormous eyebrow and a smug expression.
The Sprig knows something and will not say what it is.

title: Weeping Wumbus
sentences: Weeping Wumbus is an uncommon melon that cries Sap tears into its own pot.
Nobody should ask why the Wumbus cries.

title: The Unlicensed Carrot
sentences: The Unlicensed Carrot is a rare carrot in a tiny suit holding a briefcase that will not open.
The Carrot is not a lawyer and has never claimed to be one.

title: Sir Blombus of the Damp
sentences: Sir Blombus of the Damp is an epic knighted mushroom, visibly moist, with a tiny sword.
Sir Blombus knights nearby common plants when idle.

title: Fraudulent Orchid
aliases: two ferns in a trench coat
sentences: Fraudulent Orchid is a legendary plant that is obviously two ferns in a trench coat.
Its coat slips when it idles and nobody is supposed to look.

title: YELLING TUBER
sentences: YELLING TUBER is a mythic potato that yells and is audible across the whole village.
The Tuber can only be stolen while its owner is standing in their own lot.
